I'm setting up the Cartesian communicator with non-periodic boundaries, extracting coordinates, and using MPI_Cart_shift to find lower/upper neighbors along each axis before moving on to allocate halo buffers.\n\nWriting pack/unpack functions for ghost-cell exchange planes...\n\nI realize I need to switch box coordinates to signed integers since inclusive-range boxes could underflow with size_t when dimensions are small, so I'm using long for the box bounds and loop indices instead.\n\nNow I'm working out the shell decomposition for the padded region: peeling off k-layers (top/bottom in the 3rd dimension), then j-layers restricted to the remaining k range, then i-layers restricted to the remaining j and k ranges, leaving an inner core box as what's left after removing all outer shells.\n\nWriting mu and cnew kernel functions...\n\nNow I'm setting up the halo exchange structure with send/receive buffers per face direction, and starting the exchange routine that posts data transfers between neighboring domains.\n\nChecking the tag matching confirms the lo-to-lo and hi-to-hi sends line up correctly, and sends to PROC_NULL are safe no-ops. I just need to make sure the send buffers stay alive as vectors in the Halo struct until the waitall completes, then move on to finishing the halo exchange.\n\nAfter the waitall, I unpack each received plane into the ghost cells, or if a neighbor is PROC_NULL, I clamp the boundary by copying the adjacent interior plane instead. Then I sketch out the main timestep loop, starting the halo exchange, computing the interior mu values, finishing the halo exchange, and processing the boundary shell.\n\nStepping through the ordering, each stage's halo exchange completes before its ghost values get used downstream—mu ghosts feed into cnew's shell computation, and since the exchange overwrites every ghost plane each step, there's no risk of stale values carrying over from the previous iteration.\n\nI confirm the degenerate single-rank case works fine with PROC_NULL in the halo calls, and the packing overhead there is negligible. Then I'm sketching the gather-and-print logic: packing the interior into a flat array, computing per-rank counts and displacements from Cartesian coordinates, and using MPI_Gatherv to assemble the full field on the root rank, followed by a distributed validation routine.\n\nFor validation, I combine a NaN/Inf check with MPI_Allreduce using logical OR, then reduce min/max across ranks so every process agrees on the result. I still need to decide how to handle the empty-grid edge case—leaning toward treating it as trivially valid and skipping the min/max/NaN checks entirely, with that check placed right before the dimension-choosing step.\n\nNow I'm sketching out main(): initialize MPI, grab rank/size, parse arguments with a function that returns a status code (negative means continue, non-negative means exit immediately with that code so all ranks behave identically), restrict printing to the root rank, and finalize MPI before returning from main so stdio gets flushed naturally on exit.\n\nI'm defining the physics parameters struct and renaming the domain decomposition variable to avoid clashing with a diffusion constant also called D. Then I'm writing the chemical potential kernel, which loops over a sub-box of the grid, computes a seven-point Laplacian at each index, and combines it with the free energy derivative terms to produce mu at each point...\n\nWriting the Laplacian helper function...\n\nI need to handle halo face sizing based on decomposition lengths, and make sure the root rank for printing and gathering is consistently defined using the cart communicator's rank 0, since reordering could make it differ from world rank 0.\n\nGiven the complexity of mixing pre-cart and post-cart printing, I'll simplify by using reorder=0 so cart rank matches world rank everywhere, avoiding mismatches between the two contexts even though reorder=1 could theoretically help topology mapping on some systems.\n\nFor the empty-grid case, I'll skip cart creation entirely and treat world rank 0 as root, bypassing gather and halo logic since there's nothing to compute or exchange.\n\nI'll just wrap the actual simulation work in a check for gridSize > 0, leaving timing and performance metrics at zero otherwise, matching the original's behavior even if that produces NaN/inf in the performance numbers.\n\nNow I need to add a validation step before creating the cartesian topology: if no valid dimension decomposition is found, every rank should print the error and call MPI_Abort to terminate cleanly. Writing the physics struct and grid layout setup...\n\nWriting the face-cell iteration helper...\n\nWriting clamp copy function...\n\nI'll factor the simulation loop into a separate `runSimulation` function taking the decomposition, old/new concentration buffers, diffusion coefficient, iteration count, and communicator info, keeping timing measurement in main around the call for clarity.\n\nFor initialization I'm looping over the local interior cells, computing each point's global coordinates and a linear index, then deriving a pseudo-random starting value from that index scaled into the range [-1, 1]. For output, I gather all local pieces into a full array on the root process before writing, and timing wraps the simulation call with an MPI barrier and `MPI_Wtime` calls on either side.\n\nAfter computing elapsed seconds, I reduce the max across ranks and use that precise value (rather than truncating to integer milliseconds) to compute both the printed time and the MCUPS figure, which is cell updates divided by seconds divided by one million. The design:\n\n- 3D Cartesian decomposition with one ghost layer per face, using nonblocking halo exchange.\n- Overlap: interior cells are computed while halos are in flight.\n- Global clamped boundaries are reproduced by copying edge planes into ghosts, so the arithmetic matches the serial code.\n- Output (`-r`) is gathered to rank 0 in global order, and validation uses allreduce.","time":{"start":1792989479793,"end":1792989479836}}}
{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792989507885,"sessionID":"ses_e8981f36dffeuOmDNAcPYL7BAj","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01YW9jduZuZwHRPrpy8hDFBS","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r2/cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nnamespace {\n\nstruct Physics {\n    double dx, dy, dz;\n    double dt;\n    double e_AA, e_BB, e_AB;\n    double gamma;\n    double D;\n};\n\n// Cartesian decomposition of the global grid. Each rank owns a block of\n// len[0] x len[1] x len[2] cells starting at start[] in global coordinates.\n// Local storage is padded with one ghost layer on every side: owned cells\n// have local coordinates in [1, len], ghosts live at 0 and len+1.\nstruct Decomp {\n    int dims[3];      // process grid extents (x, y, z)\n    int coords[3];    // this rank's position in the process grid\n    int nbrLo[3];     // lower neighbour per dimension (MPI_PROC_NULL at domain edge)\n    int nbrHi[3];     // upper neighbour per dimension (MPI_PROC_NULL at domain edge)\n    size_t gn[3];     // global extents\n    size_t start[3];  // global offset of the local block\n    size_t len[3];    // local block extents\n    size_t pext[3];   // padded extents (len + 2)\n};\n\n// Balanced block partition of n items over p parts.\ninline size_t blockStart(size_t coord, size_t n, size_t p) { return coord * n / p; }\ninline size_t blockLen(size_t coord, size_t n, size_t p) { return (coord + 1) * n / p - coord * n / p; }\ninline size_t ceilDiv(size_t a, size_t b) { return (a + b - 1) / b; }\n\n// Linear index into a padded local array (x fastest, then y, then z).\ninline size_t lidx(const Decomp& dec, const size_t p[3]) {\n    return (p[2] * dec.pext[1] + p[1]) * dec.pext[0] + p[0];\n}\n\n// Choose a process grid px*py*pz == P with every extent <= the global extent,\n// so that every rank owns at least one cell. Prefer the most balanced block\n// size (minimal largest block), then the smallest halo surface.\nbool chooseDims(int P, const size_t gn[3], int dims[3]) {\n    bool found = false;\n    size_t bestVol = 0, bestSurf = 0;\n    for (int px = 1; px <= P && static_cast<size_t>(px) <= gn[0]; ++px) {\n        if (P % px != 0) continue;\n        const int rem = P / px;\n        for (int py = 1; py <= rem && static_cast<size_t>(py) <= gn[1]; ++py) {\n            if (rem % py != 0) continue;\n            const int pz = rem / py;\n            if (static_cast<size_t>(pz) > gn[2]) continue;\n            const size_t bx = ceilDiv(gn[0], px), by = ceilDiv(gn[1], py), bz = ceilDiv(gn[2], pz);\n            const size_t vol = bx * by * bz;\n            const size_t surf = bx * by + by * bz + bz * bx;\n            if (!found || vol < bestVol || (vol == bestVol && surf < bestSurf)) {\n                found = true;\n                bestVol = vol;\n                bestSurf = surf;\n                dims[0] = px;\n                dims[1] = py;\n                dims[2] = pz;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return found;\n}\n\n// Visit every owned cell of the face plane `plane` (local coordinate along d),\n// iterating over the owned extents of the two other dimensions.\ntemplate <class F>\ninline void forEachFaceCell(const Decomp& dec, int d, size_t plane, F&& fn) {\n    const int a = (d + 1) % 3, b = (d + 2) % 3;\n    size_t p[3];\n    p[d] = plane;\n    for (size_t jb = 1; jb <= dec.len[b]; ++jb) {\n        p[b] = jb;\n        for (size_t ia = 1; ia <= dec.len[a]; ++ia) {\n            p[a] = ia;\n            fn(lidx(dec, p));\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Copy plane srcPlane onto plane dstPlane along dimension d (owned extents only).\nvoid copyFacePlane(double* f, const Decomp& dec, int d, size_t dstPlane, size_t srcPlane) {\n    const int a = (d + 1) % 3, b = (d + 2) % 3;\n    size_t p[3], q[3];\n    p[d] = dstPlane;\n    q[d] = srcPlane;\n    for (size_t jb = 1; jb <= dec.len[b]; ++jb) {\n        p[b] = q[b] = jb;\n        for (size_t ia = 1; ia <= dec.len[a]; ++ia) {\n            p[a] = q[a] = ia;\n            f[lidx(dec, p)] = f[lidx(dec, q)];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\ninline size_t faceSize(const Decomp& dec, int d) {\n    return dec.len[(d + 1) % 3] * dec.len[(d + 2) % 3];\n}\n\n// Nonblocking halo exchange of one padded field. Ghost cells on a global\n// domain edge are filled from the adjacent owned plane, which reproduces the\n// clamped boundary condition of the serial code.\nstruct Halo {\n    std::array<std::vector<double>, 6> sbuf;  // index 2*d (lo face) / 2*d+1 (hi face)\n    std::array<std::vector<double>, 6> rbuf;\n    std::array<MPI_Request, 12> req;\n};\n\nvoid haloInit(const Decomp& dec, Halo& h) {\n    for (int d = 0; d < 3; ++d) {\n        const size_t n = faceSize(dec, d);\n        for (int s = 0; s < 2; ++s) {\n            h.sbuf[2 * d + s].assign(n, 0.0);\n            h.rbuf[2 * d + s].assign(n, 0.0);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid haloStart(const Decomp& dec, const double* f, Halo& h, MPI_Comm comm) {\n    int n = 0;\n    for (int d = 0; d < 3; ++d) {\n        const int count = static_cast<int>(faceSize(dec, d));\n        const int lo = dec.nbrLo[d], hi = dec.nbrHi[d];\n        // Messages travelling towards +d use tag 2d, towards -d use tag 2d+1.\n        MPI_Irecv(h.rbuf[2 * d].data(), count, MPI_DOUBLE, lo, 2 * d, comm, &h.req[n++]);\n        MPI_Irecv(h.rbuf[2 * d + 1].data(), count, MPI_DOUBLE, hi, 2 * d + 1, comm, &h.req[n++]);\n\n        double* sHi = h.sbuf[2 * d + 1].data();\n        size_t pos = 0;\n        forEachFaceCell(dec, d, dec.len[d], [&](size_t idx) { sHi[pos++] = f[idx]; });\n        MPI_Isend(sHi, count, MPI_DOUBLE, hi, 2 * d, comm, &h.req[n++]);\n\n        double* sLo = h.sbuf[2 * d].data();\n        pos = 0;\n        forEachFaceCell(dec, d, 1, [&](size_t idx) { sLo[pos++] = f[idx]; });\n        MPI_Isend(sLo, count, MPI_DOUBLE, lo, 2 * d + 1, comm, &h.req[n++]);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid haloFinish(const Decomp& dec, double* f, Halo& h) {\n    MPI_Waitall(12, h.req.data(), MPI_STATUSES_IGNORE);\n    for (int d = 0; d < 3; ++d) {\n        const size_t hiGhost = dec.len[d] + 1;\n        if (dec.nbrLo[d] != MPI_PROC_NULL) {\n            const double* r = h.rbuf[2 * d].data();\n            size_t pos = 0;\n            forEachFaceCell(dec, d, 0, [&](size_t idx) { f[idx] = r[pos++]; });\n        } else {\n            copyFacePlane(f, dec, d, 0, 1);\n        }\n        if (dec.nbrHi[d] != MPI_PROC_NULL) {\n            const double* r = h.rbuf[2 * d + 1].data();\n            size_t pos = 0;\n            forEachFaceCell(dec, d, hiGhost, [&](size_t idx) { f[idx] = r[pos++]; });\n        } else {\n            copyFacePlane(f, dec, d, hiGhost, dec.len[d]);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Inclusive box of padded local coordinates (signed to allow empty boxes).\nstruct Box {\n    long i0, i1, j0, j1, k0, k1;\n};\n\n// Owned cells whose 7-point stencil touches no ghost cell.\nBox innerBox(const Decomp& dec) {\n    return Box{2, static_cast<long>(dec.len[0]) - 1,\n               2, static_cast<long>(dec.len[1]) - 1,\n               2, static_cast<long>(dec.len[2]) - 1};\n}\n\n// Owned cells on the surface of the block. The fix would be to size the process grid to the largest product ≤ P and idle the leftover ranks, splitting the communicator so active ranks form the cartesian grid while idle ranks still participate in barriers, reductions, and gathers using the world communicator with neutral contributions.\n\nMaximizing product does pick the exact factorization P whenever it exists, confirming this is the right objective. For the search itself, I'd loop over divisor candidates for px and py, then set pz to the largest value satisfying both the grid dimension limit and the remaining budget, though I need to be careful since pz doesn't have to be an exact divisor to still maximize the product.\n\nEven the degenerate case of a single cell with multiple ranks works fine, leaving one active rank and the rest idle, so chooseDims never fails as long as grid size is positive. Now I'm sketching the implementation: having chooseDims return the active count, then splitting the communicator based on whether a rank falls below that active threshold.\n\nWith reorder disabled, active ranks preserve their world rank ordering within the new communicator, so the active subcomm rank matches world rank for ranks below the active count. Idle ranks get MPI_COMM_NULL and skip the grid work entirely, but still need to participate in the barrier, the reduce for max seconds (contributing zero), and the validation allreduce on the world communicator (contributing an identity value), with rank 0 as root for gathering and printing results. I'm restructuring main to split off a working communicator accordingly.\n\nFor the validation step, idle ranks need to feed in a zero bad-count and extreme min/max sentinel values (positive and negative infinity) so they don't skew the reduction across the world communicator.\n\nThat min/max logic checks out with real data. For gatherField, idle ranks shouldn't call it since gathering happens on the work communicator, so I need to guard that call with an active-rank check, while printResults stays root-only.\n\nDims product must equal the number of active ranks for Cart_create to work on the work comm, which it does by construction, so the \"cannot decompose\" error path becomes unreachable. I need to revise chooseDims to maximize the product, restructure main accordingly, include the limits header for infinity, and simplify validateDistributed's signature to drop the extra flag.\n\n","time":{"start":1792989752109,"end":1792989770012},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
